clue.text: Worker on edge for hymn  ...

blocks.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect
a hem is the finished edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A labourer perched on a ledge is offered a hymn, the dots carrying the thought into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the worker in front of the edge. The trailing dots hand the same worker to the next clue, which pairs it with a different edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a solemn choral song of praise, often sung in church, which is exactly what a hymn is.

clue.text: Navy high flier or red delicate flier

definitions.note: the red admiral is the butterfly; red is part of its name

blocks.note: first meaning: a naval officer of the highest rank, a high flier in the navy
second meaning: the red ..., a common butterfly

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer is compared with a fragile red insect on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' suggests an aviator, but here it is a person at the top of a career; the second flier really does fly, as a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The top rank in a navy is that title, and the red admiral is a familiar European butterfly sharing the name.

clue.text: Pulse in broth

indicators.note: read as 'in a stew', so the following word is in a jumbled state

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lentils or beans floating in soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like the edible seed that goes into broth, but it is the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, like the pulse felt at the wrist or temple.

clue.text: Hat almost upside-down the French will honour

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the headwear is dropped
in a down entry, turning something upside-down reads it from the bottom up

blocks.note: a bonnet is a kind of hat
le is the French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone wearing an upturned hat is promised an honour by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upside-down' means reading from the bottom up; 'almost' acts on the hat before it is flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, conferring a title, which is a way of honouring them.

clue.text: ...  or Irish county

blocks.note: the dots carry over 'Worker' from the previous clue, and the worker is the ant
the dots also carry over 'edge', here read as a rim

explanation.surface: The clue completes the previous one: a worker on the edge, for a hymn or for an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay lives in the previous clue: 'Worker on edge' again, but this time the edge is a different synonym. Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in the north-east of the island, home of the Giant's Causeway.

clue.text: Observing naught is heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is taken away

blocks.note: naught means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that watching nothing at all is cold and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTHING has seven letters, and its middle one, H, is the heart removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means taking notice of or perceiving something, so it can replace observing in a sentence like 'noting the change'.

clue.text: Possums' call, the reverse call

blocks.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them
when a coin is tossed you call heads or its opposite, the reverse face

explanation.surface: It sounds like a description of the cry possums make, and then their cry backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like an instruction to turn letters round, but the reverse of a coin is its tails side, the other call in a toss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringtails are possums of Australia and New Guinea, named for their curling prehensile tails used for gripping branches.

clue.text: Girl minded by married woman should exhibit good behaviour

indicators.note: someone minded is looked after, kept safely within another's care

blocks.note: a girl's name
Mrs is the title of a married woman

explanation.surface: A girl looked after by a wife ought to behave well.
explanation.definitionFit: Manners are polite social conduct, the courteous ways of behaving that a well brought up child is expected to show.

clue.text: Marriage without love: inform the single man that's stupid

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter standing for love is left out

blocks.note: a marriage is a union
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to inform someone is to tell them
single means one, the Roman numeral I
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A loveless marriage, and someone tells the bachelor how foolish he is.
explanation.walkthrough: UNION loses one O to give UNIN; the rest is laid on in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligent means lacking intelligence or good sense, a plain synonym for dim or foolish.

clue.text: Once the highest position for an Afghan was a space station

definitions.text: Once the highest position for an Afghan

blocks.note: taken as written
Mir was the Russian space station in orbit from 1986 to 2001

explanation.surface: A history note: the top job in Afghanistan was once out in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Amir, a form of emir, was the title of the rulers of Afghanistan until the early twentieth century, when kings replaced them.

clue.text: See 12
No Eton rower when born by right enters backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the words for the newborn's companion and the side are read from the end
something that enters goes inside, so it sits within the other piece

blocks.note: DOB is the abbreviation for date of birth, when one was born
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An Eton boy who does not row, born to the right sort and making his way backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: At Eton College a dry bob is a boy who plays cricket rather than rowing; a rower is a wet bob. Only 'by right' goes backwards, not the date of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton slang divides pupils into wet bobs, who row, and dry bobs, who take up cricket and other land sports instead.

clue.text: Now mostly mime in capitals

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes
Roman numerals are written in capital letters, so the word is read as a number

blocks.note: cut short by a letter, this word becomes MIM, three Roman numerals read together as a year: M, then IM for a thousand less one

explanation.surface: An actor in a city performs silently, for the moment mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in 1999, so 'Now' is that year. MIM is a loose Roman form, M plus IM (a thousand less one).
explanation.definitionFit: For the original solvers the present year was the one in the answer, so 'now' named the current date when this was published.

clue.text: Burdened dragging pole, so rested

indicators.note: one thing dragging another pulls it along behind, so it comes first in the line

blocks.note: S is the south pole, one of the compass points
to be lumbered with something is to be burdened by it

explanation.surface: Someone weighed down by hauling a long pole lies down to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burdened dragging pole' reads as the burdened word pulling the pole, but the pole leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumbered is the past tense of slumber, to sleep, and sleeping is resting.

clue.text: Pre-election promises make some faint

indicators.note: to make something is to build it up, here from the following letters rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wry political joke: party pledges are enough to make some voters swoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a party's published statement of its policies, issued before an election to win votes.

clue.text: A little peck is seen here

definitions.text: A little peck is seen here

indicators.note: here points at the words in front of you, telling you to look within them for the letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A tender moment: a quick peck spotted somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a little peck, and the answer sits inside 'peck is seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peck is a quick light touch of the lips, a small brief one of the affectionate kind given on the cheek.

clue.text: It's common to ponder for an informer

indicators.note: common here means a working-class London accent, which turns a th sound into an f

blocks.note: to ponder is to think, and in Cockney speech the th of that word comes out as an f

explanation.surface: Someone muses that it is vulgar to deliberate about turning informer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the London working-class accent, swaps th for f.
explanation.definitionFit: Fink is American slang for an informer or stool pigeon who tells tales to the police or bosses.

clue.text: Lying down as fast as possible

blocks.note: first meaning: stretched out horizontally, prone
second meaning: at full speed, with maximum effort

explanation.surface: A paradox: lying down while going at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone sprawled full length, and also an engine or runner going at full throttle.

clue.text: Artist destroyed "Lost Dream"

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the quoted letters are smashed and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter wrecked a canvas titled Lost Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter from before about 1800, such as Rembrandt or Titian, so certainly an artist.

clue.text: French entertainer's camera work for Universal

indicators.note: putting something to work reshapes it, so the preceding word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the British film classification for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A French performer is filmed for the Universal studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' poses as the Hollywood studio; it is the U film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Marceau was the famous French mime artist, creator of the white-faced clown Bip, a celebrated stage entertainer.

clue.text: Savouring cream for energy, settled on one's top of the milk

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a bird that has settled on a branch has lit there
one is I, plus the 's
the initial letter of milk

explanation.surface: Enjoying the cream that rises to the top of the milk, for a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' and 'top of the milk' seem dairy, but the cream is the social elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief in, or relish for, rule by a select few, the cream of society enjoying superiority.

clue.text: Twenty-one shillings for fowl  ...

definitions.note: the full name is guinea fowl

blocks.note: first meaning: the old British coin and sum worth one pound and one shilling
second meaning: the first word of the name of a speckled African game bird

explanation.surface: Paying a large sum in old money for a bird, the dots leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 Britain counted twenty shillings to the pound; the coin worth a shilling more was used for fees and horse prices.
explanation.definitionFit: The old coin was worth exactly that sum, and the guinea fowl is a farmyard game bird from West Africa.

clue.text: German tennis player about to take money in sport is well off!

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the player's name is read from the end
taking something in means holding it within, so the other piece goes inside
in places the cash letter inside the word for amusement

blocks.note: Steffi Graf, the German champion
L is the pound sign, standing for money
sport in the sense of fun, as in 'just for sport'

explanation.surface: A rich German tennis star turning to money in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well off' suggests wealth, but means distant. L goes into FUN, and that goes into FARG.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-flung means remote or distant, a long way away, which is what 'well off' means read as 'a good distance away'.

clue.text: One speeds, say, in the country

indicators.note: say asks you to pronounce the phrase and listen to the result

blocks.note: one who speeds is a rusher, said with a non-rhotic British accent

explanation.surface: Someone races along out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech the final r of rusher is silent, so it matches the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the largest country in the world, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

clue.text: ... or mollusc

blocks.note: the dots carry over 'Twenty-one shillings' from the previous clue; S is a shilling
the other twenty shillings make a pound, called a quid

explanation.surface: The clue finishes the previous one: twenty-one shillings for a fowl, or for a mollusc.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the previous clue's 'Twenty-one shillings', split as one shilling plus a pound; S abbreviates shilling and quid is slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A squid is a ten-armed cephalopod, and cephalopods belong to the mollusc group along with snails and octopuses.

clue.text: Correspondence with letters reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: letters other than vowels

explanation.surface: Exchanging letters by post, as told to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' and 'letters' both suggest the post; here the first means agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonance is harmony or agreement, and correspondence can mean agreement between things, as in a match of ideas.

clue.text: The whole thing can turn around

indicators.note: turning around means facing the other way, so the pieces are read from the end

blocks.note: a tin is a can
a U-turn, so turn gives U

explanation.surface: A boast that the whole contraption can rotate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb, but it is the metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single complete entity, one whole thing regarded as an individual piece.

clue.text: So-called model horse just originally concealed?

definitions.text: So-called model horse just originally concealed?

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the first letter is kept
something concealed is hidden inside something else

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
a roan is a horse with a mixed coat
the first letter of just

explanation.surface: The famous wooden horse was supposedly a model with soldiers hidden inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the wooden horse of Troy, a model horse with Greeks concealed in it; J goes inside ROAN after T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan horse was a hollow wooden horse, an offering that hid Greek soldiers, so a model horse with men concealed.

clue.text: Exploding bullet sounds doubly 8

indicators.note: sounds means the cross-referenced word is spoken, so only its pronunciation matters

blocks.note: 8 is a word meaning stupid; said twice, with its silent final letter

explanation.surface: An exploding bullet that makes a sound twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is UNINTELLIGENT, meaning dumb; dumb said twice gives the bullet's name, since the B is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumdum is a soft-nosed bullet that expands on impact, named after the Indian arsenal at Dum Dum.
